anya: Heads-up: canary for model v2 on /api/chat showed ~2.3x P99 token latency bump starting ~13:12 UTC. Seems correlated with kernel fallback and a shift in batchshape distribution. Posting quick notes.
chris: Ugh. Do you have sampled traces or flame graphs? which kernel fell back?
anya: I pulled 50 sampled traces from the canary window. Most traces show kernel selection switching from `fast_attn_quant` -> `fallback_attn` once sequence length > 128 and batchshape includes many short-seq requests. KV cache hit rate for v2 during the window dropped from 98% -> 74%.
anya: paste:```
# observed rollout policy (canary 10%)
model_versions:
  - name: v1
    kernel_pref: fast_attn_quant
  - name: v2
    kernel_pref: fast_attn_quant
fallbacks:
  seq_len_threshold: 128
  kernel_fallback: fallback_attn
```
chris: Hmm kernel fallback on seq len threshold is expected but why KV hit rate drop? Are we evicting prefixes or mis-attributing cache keys?
devon: @anya can you share an example request distribution? maybe v2 changed tokenization -> different prefix keys. Also any change to batching heuristics?
anya: Distribution snippet: 60% short (<32) + 30% mid (32-128) + 10% long (>128). On v1, batching heuristics grouped short requests into larger microbatches; on v2 we see many short+long mixes that force smaller effective batch shapes and trigger fallback kernels.
anya: Quick grep from traces: many cache miss logs like `kvcache: miss key=<prefix-hash> not-found` for requests that should've hit. No recent K/V eviction policy changes.
perf-bot: alert: route=/api/chat P99_token_latency increased to 210ms (baseline 92ms) on canary group v2 at 1967894321. Threshold 150ms.
chris: Could be two orthogonal issues: (1) batching microshapes causing kernel selection mismatch (slower path), (2) tokenization or request id variance causing new cache keys. Both multiply.
devon: For dashboards: we should add a per-route panel that breaks down token-level latency by kernel selected + kvcache_hit boolean and by model_version. Query idea: `avg(token_latency) by kernel, kvcache_hit, model_version, route` and a stacked P90/P99. Also add a heatmap of batchshape (batch_size x avg_seq_len) over time.
anya: Agreed. I also exported sampled traces to s3://redwood-perf/canaries/1967894321/traces-50.json and a mini flame excerpt in the thread.
anya: Quick mitigation I spun up: bumped canary routing to 5% and forced v2 kernel_pref to `fast_attn_quant` via override to see if selection change helps; initial result: P99 back down to ~130ms but KV hit still low.
chris: Nice. Next: compare tokenizer outputs for identical inputs between v1/v2 to confirm prefix hash divergence. If tokenizer changed, we'll need cache key compatibility or mapping.
devon: I'll add dashboard panels and an alert rule: fire if model_version CANARY has simultaneous kernel_fallback rate > 5% AND kvcache_hit_rate < 85% for 5m. Will also add a short-term watchlist to the rollout page.
anya: Action items: 1) chris -> diff tokenizer for v1/v2 and post findings (ETA 2h). 2) devon -> add kernel+kv panels and batchshape heatmap (ETA 1h). 3) anya -> rerun canary with token-prefix-compat shim and collect 200 traces (ETA 3h).
chris: I'll also check kernel selector heuristics: maybe we need a per-model override for batchshape thresholds to avoid fallback for mixed batches.
anya: thanks — will keep updating here. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: note: automated rollback window scheduled in 30m unless canary metrics return to baseline.
